hints: Focus on symmetry of each C=C bond, since a symmetric C=C gives one place for Br while an unsymmetric C=C gives two.
Notice the middle C=C has identical $\text{CH}_2$-ring groups on both sides, but each cyclohexene C=C has the side-chain closer to one end of the double bond.
Consider what happens to the middle of the molecule when the two end rings end up the same versus different, and how that affects where the middle Br can go.
walkthrough:
**Identify the three alkene sites**

Molecule X has one central chain $\text{C=C}$ and two ring $\text{C=C}$ bonds. All three each add one $\text{HBr}$ because 1 mol X reacts with 3 mol $\text{HBr}$.

$$\text{C=C + HBr} \rightarrow \text{CH-CBr}$$

**Check the central C=C for symmetry**

The centre is $\text{R-CH}_2\text{-CH=CH-CH}_2\text{-R}$ where R is the cyclohexenyl ring. Both sides are identical, so putting Br on the left C or the right C gives the same connectivity. This centre alone gives 1 structural pattern.

**Check each ring C=C for symmetry**

Each ring is a substituted cyclohexene with the $\text{CH}_2$ side-chain in an unsymmetric position relative to the double bond. Protonating one end versus the other end puts the $\text{Br}$ on different ring carbons. So each ring alone has 2 structural possibilities, call them type 1 and type 2.

**Combine the two identical rings**

The left and right rings start identical. So for the pair we get only 3 distinct combinations: 1-1, 2-2, and 1-2. The 1-2 and 2-1 pair are identical by flipping the whole molecule end to end.

**Add the effect on the central Br**

If the two ends are the same (1-1 or 2-2), the molecule stays left-right symmetric, so central Br left or right is still the same. That gives 2 products. If the ends are different (1-2), left and right are no longer identical, so Br nearer the type-1 end is structurally different from Br nearer the type-2 end. That gives 2 more products. Total is $2 + 2 = 4$.

options.A: 3 counts only the 1-1, 2-2 and 1-2 ring combinations and forgets that the 1-2 case makes the two sides of the central chain different, splitting the central Br position into two distinct structures.
options.B: Correct. Each unsymmetric ring gives 2 Br positions. Identical rings give 3 pairings. Two pairings with same ends give 1 central pattern each, while the mixed pairing gives 2 central patterns, giving 4 structural products in total.
options.C: 6 comes from incorrectly multiplying 2 x 3 or 2 x 2 + 2 without allowing for the end-to-end symmetry of X. The 1-2 ring combination is the same as 2-1, so you overcount if you treat left and right rings as fully independent.
options.D: 8 comes from treating all three C=C bonds as independent and unsymmetric with $2 \times 2 \times 2 = 8$. This ignores that the central C=C is symmetric and that the two end rings are identical to each other, which greatly reduces duplicates.
